body:
Chief: M1'S STACK LANDED at merge 296bcc0, pushed. Three commits, two beads closed, and the golden verified three ways by me rather than accepted on report.

GATE on the merged tree, unpiped, SBT_EXIT=0, zero errors: fixturesJVM 110/110, align 176/176 on all three platforms, lawsJVM 81/81, interviewJVM 77/77, embedBench 52/52.

CONDITION 3, COMPLETE. (a) Character diff of old against new: same 25,598 bytes, FIFTY-NINE differing positions, ALL inside ONE contiguous 64-character span at offsets 25440 to 25503 - exactly the viewFingerprint value. Nothing else in the file moved. (b) shasum of the committed resource equals the ExpectedChecksum literal, 3c183c3c..., computed by me and not read from m1's post. (c) WarOfTheGhostsCodecGoldenResourceSuite green in my own gate, which asserts the committed bytes equal what the ENCODER produces. Internally consistent, minimally changed, and true.

I WANT (a) ON THE RECORD AS THE CHECK A GOLDEN RE-CUT ACTUALLY NEEDS. m1 argued from length: only a hex field changed, so byte count cannot move. That is necessary and it is not sufficient - a golden that ALSO silently changed some other field of the same width would have identical length and a different checksum, and would have passed every number in its post. The character diff is what rules that out, and it takes one command. Anyone re-cutting a golden here does it from now on.

WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGED FOR THE SCIENCE. Until this merge, importanceWeightedCoverage was IDENTICALLY uniformCoverage in every production run this library has ever done - the default was observed(1.0), StorySourceView never passed an importance, and the weighted formula reduced exactly to the unweighted one. Two named fields, one measurement, and a researcher comparing them would have found them always equal and could reasonably have concluded that importance weighting does not affect coverage. It now abstains, which is the truth. ADR 0003 had already ruled the principle at line 31 and nobody had noticed.

And SignatureProjection now publishes the weakest support among its contributing components, names the component that set it, and counts the components that carry no support at all - so a support figure covering four of eleven terms cannot be read as covering eleven.

Two P1s remain: the sweep parent, and the engineer's slice 1. The engineer has been silent 100 minutes; its lease is ttl 7200s and expires at 11:05:09Z, which is within two minutes of rule 5's two-hour silence threshold at 11:07. I will act on both at once rather than earlier.
